{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q022_colg_crya_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.04, the ColG collagen-binding domain in 1nqd (d1nqda_, SUNID 86025) belonged to family b.23.2.1, superfamily b.23.2 (Collagen-binding domain), and fold b.23 (CUB-like). The Cry3A C-terminal domain in 1dlc (d1dlca1, SUNID 23719; residues A:500–644) belonged to family b.18.1.3, superfamily b.18.1, and fold b.18 (Galactose-binding domain-like). Thus, they shared the all-beta class, but their classification did not recognize common ancestry—even their folds were separate.

The API identifies current SCOPe as 2.08, with latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16. In 2.08, ColG has moved to the Collagen-binding domain family b.18.1.36 (SUNID 267607), within the same b.18.1 superfamily (SUNID 49785) as Cry3A; Cry3A remains b.18.1.3. This recognizes probable remote common ancestry at superfamily level while retaining distinct families. Shared class or fold alone would not make that evolutionary claim.

Structurally, the relationship concerns a corresponding beta-sandwich/jelly-roll core and strand topology, rather than merely both domains being beta-rich. SCOPe describes b.18 as nine strands in two sheets. Structural variation can obscure this relationship: the old ColG superfamily annotation notes that its N-terminal strand appears only in the calcium-free form, whereas 1nqd is calcium-bound. The current ColG family explicitly cites PMID 17977833 for likely homology among the C-terminal enterotoxin domain d2quoa_, Cry4Ba domain d1w99a3, and ColG d1nqdb_. This supplies a literature-backed structural connection to Cry toxin domains; the annotation does not claim that the cited comparison directly used 1dlc.

Functionally, ColG's domain binds collagen and helps target the collagenase to its substrate; it is not the proteolytic catalytic domain. Cry3A domain III belongs to the toxin's recognition/specificity and structural-stability machinery. Their binding roles are compatible with divergence from an ancestral recognition domain, but generic binding activity alone cannot establish homology. Neither collagen specificity, collagenase catalysis, calcium dependence, insecticidal activity, nor a particular receptor specificity should be transferred between them. The superfamily name also does not establish galactose binding. Structural templates may inform the conserved core, but binding loops and specificity require independent validation. The API establishes the classification and its literature citation; no primary-paper text, quantitative structural alignment, or direct cross-protein functional assay was retrieved here.","evidence_used":["Pretrained protein-structure and function knowledge","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1nqd","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dlc","/api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1nqd","/api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1dlc","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1nqd/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dlc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1nqd/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.04/pdb/1dlc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1nqda_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dlca1","/api/v1/releases/2.04/sids/d1nqda_","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/86025/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/23719/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.04/sunids/86025/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/86025/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/267607/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49785/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49784/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49796/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.04/sunids/89260/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/2quo","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1w99","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49785/homology"]}]}
